title: Review — jsrepo
story:
Proof-carrying review — jsrepo

ignore free items
2 files analysed (.md×1, .js×1). Nothing from the repository was executed except its own test command. Step through to see how the review grows from the diff to its history and to the code that mentions it.
captions: What a reviewer sees: 2 changed files. Question: what does this change quietly rely on? With the diff alone there is nothing to label: 0 findings.
The change makes claims (amber): that its symbols are tested, and any absolute sentence it adds to the docs. Not checked yet, so unlabeled.
History is evidence. 1 earlier commits touched these files, and 0 file(s) habitually change with them. The graph pulls them in (dashed). Habits are induced, so they stay Unknown: leads, not proof.
A text search finds 1 place(s) that mention the changed code and 0 that mention those (pink). These are listed to look at, not assumed broken.
Each claim ends Refuted (counterexample in the text or a failing run), Tested, Proved within scope, or Unknown. Here: 1 refuted. The human decision stays pending.

pend: The AI lists evidence and leads. It cannot approve this change, and most of what it lists is Unknown by design.

claims.claim: Every symbol this change touches is mentioned by at least one test file.
claims.origin: derived from the diff and a text search of the repository
claims.plain: Does anything in the test suite even mention the code this change touches?
claims.formula: ∀ s ∈ CHANGED_SYMBOLS. a test file mentions s
claims.label: Proved within scope
assumptions: symbols are extracted by pattern (not a parser); 'mentions' means a whole-word text match in a test file

claims.short: doc: Totals are always positive a…
claims.claim: README.md:3 says: "Totals are always positive and never include refunds."
claims.plain: A sentence with an absolute word (never/always/only/…) was added. No test reads documentation.
claims.label: Unknown
claims.note: no automatic checker can verify a prose claim; a person (or a --spec command) must.

claims.claim: receipt() in src/receipt.js keeps behaving correctly after total() changed.
claims.origin: receipt() mentions `total` at src/receipt.js:3 (text match, 1 hop from the change)
claims.plain: receipt() uses code this change touches. It is a place to look, not a proven problem.
claims.label: Unknown
claims.note: no checker available: listed because it mentions the changed code. Add a --spec command to test it.

claims.claim: The project's own tests pass on the changed code.
claims.label: Tested
claims.scope_note: A pass means these tests passed once, on this machine. Other inputs may still fail.

claims.claim: A refund line (negative price) is still summed into the total
claims.plain: A refund line (negative price) is still summed into the total
claims.label: Refuted
claims.scope_note: The command passed on this checkout once; other inputs may still fail.

claims.short: the change is what was intended
claims.claim: This change does what its author and the requirement intended.
claims.plain: Whether the change matches the intent behind it is a human judgement.
claims.label: Unknown
claims.note: a question of intent; code cannot decide it.

rules.R-RUN: A claim is only Tested or Refuted because something was executed.
rules.R-STATIC: A claim about the code text can be refuted by a counterexample found in the text, under listed assumptions.
rules.R-HIST: Earlier changes to the same files are evidence about what this change should also touch.
rules.R-CALL: If a function changes, every function that mentions it is a place to look; they are listed, not assumed broken.
rules.R-DOC: A sentence in the docs makes a claim that no test reads.
rules.R-HUMAN: Questions of intent cannot be decided by code. They go to a person.
